title: Linked List Cycle
statement:
Given the `head` of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle in it.

There is a cycle in a linked list if some node in the list can be reached again by continuously following the `next` pointer. Internally, `pos` denotes the index of the node that the tail's `next` pointer connects to (`-1` means there is no cycle).

Return `true` if there is a cycle, or `false` otherwise. Build the list from `values`, wire the tail's `next` to node `pos` when `pos !== -1`, then detect the cycle with Floyd's slow/fast pointer technique (do not rely on visited-set techniques that would need to store node references beyond this call).
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4]
pos is -1 or a valid index in the linked list

examples.explanation: The tail connects to the node at index 1 (value 2), forming a cycle.

editorial.approach: Use two pointers, `slow` (moves one step at a time) and `fast` (moves two steps at a time), both starting at `head`. If there is no cycle, `fast` (or `fast.next`) will reach `null` and you can return false. If there is a cycle, `fast` will eventually lap `slow` and they will point to the same node — return true as soon as that happens.
